About Us

We are a technical duo combining software/systems development and telecommunications engineering, focused on tackling the Dancing with the SARs challenge. Our background brings together RF and electromagnetic signal fundamentals (radio waves, frequency bands, backscatter physics) and backend automation/data pipelines (Python, data processing, and scripting).
summary: Biobío SAR Monitor is an interactive web GIS platform that combines multi-sensor Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) imagery from NASA's NISAR (L-band) and ESA's Sentinel-1 (C-band) to detect and measure flood extents through heavy cloud cover in Chile's Biobío Region. While dense storm clouds blind optical satellites, SAR sensors penetrate weather day and night. Using Python, raw acquisitions are radiometrically calibrated to decibels (dB), reprojected to WGS 84 (EPSG:4326), and analyzed via multi-temporal change detection across real flood events (June 2024 and September 2026, validated with 32.8 mm of rainfall at Carriel Sur). By subtracting pre-storm baselines from storm dates, the map highlights new open-water flooding in red and sub-canopy inundation beneath forests in cyan, filtering out permanent water bodies. Built with Leaflet.js for desktop and mobile use, it features opacity controls, rapid navigation to critical areas like Tubul and the Biobío River mouth, and a spherical geodesic ruler to measure flooded perimeter and hectares in real time.
details:
What It Does & How It Works

Biobío SAR Monitor is a lightweight web GIS platform designed to detect, visualize, and quantify flood extents through dense cloud cover in Chile's Biobío Region. Our processing pipeline works in three stages:

1. Radiometric Calibration & Georeferencing: Raw Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) acquisitions from NASA's NISAR (L-band) and ESA's Sentinel-1 (C-band) are calibrated into decibels (dB), reprojected to WGS 84 (EPSG:4326), and clipped to the Biobío coastal and river basin (-73.60° to -72.70° W, -37.70° to -36.50° S).

2. Multi-Temporal Change Detection: By subtracting dry pre-storm baselines from storm acquisitions pixel-by-pixel, the algorithm isolates new inundation while filtering out permanent ocean and river bodies. Open-water flooding (specular reflection drop) is mapped in red, while water trapped beneath vegetation and forestry plantations (L-band double-bounce backscatter increase) is mapped in cyan.

3. Interactive Web Visualization & Measurement: Processed layers are served as georeferenced transparent overlays on an interactive Leaflet.js map featuring opacity sliders, quick-jump presets to vulnerable zones (Tubul wetlands and the Biobío River mouth), and a spherical geodesic ruler that calculates affected perimeter (km) and surface area (hectares and km²) in real time.

Creativity & Key Factors Considered

Rather than relying on a single sensor, our core creative approach was pairing two complementary radar wavelengths ("dancing" C-band and L-band) to overcome southern Chile's dense forestry and wetland canopy cover, where single-band optical or C-band sensors often miss sub-canopy flooding. We validated our detection windows against real local events—the June 2024 river overflows and the September 2026 frontal storm confirmed by 32.8 mm of precipitation recorded at Carriel Sur meteorological station. We also prioritized field accessibility by pre-rendering lightweight overlays and designing a responsive mobile interface so emergency personnel can take geodesic measurements directly from a smartphone without specialized GIS software or high bandwidth.

Benefits & Intended Impact

During severe frontal storms, cloud cover blinds optical satellites precisely when local responders need situational awareness most. Biobío SAR Monitor bridges the gap between raw spaceborne radar science and rapid local decision-making, empowering municipal emergency teams and disaster response agencies (such as SENAPRED) to identify flooded infrastructure and estimate affected hectares within seconds.

Tools, Languages & Software Used

- Data Processing & Scientific Analysis: Python (rasterio, h5py, numpy, matplotlib)

- Web Frontend & Geospatial Engine: HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, Leaflet.js, OpenStreetMap & ESRI World Imagery basemaps

- Hosting & Version Control: GitHub & GitHub Pages

- Source Code Repository: https://github.com/matiaspvSOC/SAR_Monitor_SpaceApp
